title: Creamy Rosé Penne
subtitle: penne in a silky pink tomato-cream sauce with garlic and Parmesan, the Canadian restaurant favourite
imageAlt: A bowl of penne in a creamy pink rosé sauce with grated Parmesan on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Save a cup of pasta water before draining; it makes the sauce glossy.

steps.title: Water on
steps.text: Bring a big pot of water to a boil with the salt.

steps.title: Base
steps.text: Melt the butter in a large deep skillet over medium. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the tomato paste for 1 minute, stirring.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, Italian seasoning, sugar, salt and pepper and simmer 10 minutes, stirring now and then.

steps.title: Pasta
steps.text: Meanwhile, cook the penne 1 minute less than the package says. Scoop out 1 cup of the water, then drain.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: Stir the cream into the sauce and bring to a gentle simmer, then stir in the Parmesan until smooth.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the penne and toss 1 minute over low, adding pasta water a splash at a time until glossy.

fixIt.fix: Add another pinch of sugar or a splash more cream.
Loosen with pasta water a little at a time.
It boiled too hard. Take it off the heat and stir in a splash of cold cream.

saleTip: Crushed tomatoes and penne are regular No Frills loss leaders; stock up at $1.49 and $1.
swap: Half-and-half (10%) for the cream: simmer gently and don't boil. Rigatoni or rotini for penne.
leftovers: The pasta soaks up sauce overnight; add a splash of milk when reheating.
doneness: Meatless. Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada, leftovers).
source: Based on tested rosé sauce methods (Ricardo, Canadian Living): a garlic-tomato sauce finished with whipping cream and Parmesan.
prepAhead: Make the tomato base up to 3 days ahead; add the cream when reheating.
reheat: Covered in the microwave with a splash of milk, 2–3 minutes, stirring halfway, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Garlic tomato cream with Parmesan; no onion or Italian seasoning.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the onion; just the garlic and tomato paste.

fancy.note: Browned mild Italian sausage folded through.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: first brown the sausage meat in the skillet, breaking it up, 7–8 minutes until no pink remains and 71°C (160°F); lift it out, then cook the onion in the fat.

addSteps.title: Sausage
addSteps.text: Stir the sausage back in with the cream.

plating: Twist the penne into shallow bowls.
Extra Parmesan grated over the top.

why.1-9: Whipping cream won't curdle in the acidic tomatoes the way milk can.
why.1-3: Cooking the paste first deepens the tomato flavour.
why.1-6: A little sugar rounds off the tang of canned tomatoes.

funFact: Rosé sauce is mostly a Canadian and North American restaurant name; in Italy a similar sauce is called 'salsa rosa'.
drink: A dry rosé, or sparkling pink lemonade.
